sources_considered.why: Stanford-led study (FAccT 2023, first posted November 2022) documenting stereotypes in text-to-image models.
Reuters report on the Getty v. Stability AI training-data lawsuit and the related artists' class action.

receipt.public_excerpt: We find a broad range of ordinary prompts produce stereotypes, including prompts simply mentioning traits, descriptors, occupations, or objects.

evidence_items.explanation: Research first posted in November 2022 found widespread racial and gender stereotyping in popular text-to-image models. That supports the bias half of the claim.

receipt.public_excerpt: Getty Images has sued artificial intelligence company Stability AI Inc, accusing it in a lawsuit made public on Monday of misusing more than 12 million Getty photos to train its Stable Diffusion AI image-generation system.

evidence_items.explanation: A major copyright lawsuit over training data was filed days before the post. That supports the copyright half of the claim.

receipt.public_excerpt: follows a separate Getty case against Stability in the United Kingdom and a related class-action complaint filed by artists in California against Stability and other companies in the fast-growing field of generative AI.

evidence_items.explanation: By the time of the post there were several training-data copyright suits in two countries. This shows the disputes were broad, not isolated.

receipt.public_excerpt: His decision said Anthropic’s use of the books to train its models, including versions of its flagship AI model Claude, was “exceedingly transformative” enough to fall under fair use.

evidence_items.explanation: A 2025 US ruling found that training on lawfully obtained books was fair use, though pirated copies were not. This weakens a reading in which training itself is legally infringement. It falls outside the target period.

unresolved_gaps: The bias study documents biased outputs but does not prove those biases come only from training data.
Whether training is legally infringement remains unsettled across jurisdictions. The verdict here rests on the existence of serious disputes, not on court outcomes.
